main.title: Golden Joystick Awards 2020
main.summary: The Golden Joystick Awards, with every category winner of the 2020 edition.

cards.heading: The players' awards
cards.text: The Golden Joystick Awards celebrate games through a public vote, bringing players into the choice of each year's winners. The awards began in Britain with the 1983 season and later reached an international audience through online voting. Their changing categories trace the growth of games: home computers and consoles, handhelds, online play, independent studios, performance and music. Alongside the public vote, special honours recognise individual contributions to the industry. Each edition preserves its own category names, so the results also show what players and the awards organisers considered worth celebrating at the time.

main.title: Anthology of the Killer
main.subtitle: The series begins with Voice of the Killer
main.summary: Anthology of the Killer is a series and collection of nine horror comedy games that were developed by Irish independent game developer Stephen Gillmurphy under the pseudonyms "garmentdistrict" and "thecatamites".

cards.heading: From the first free episode to a nine-game collection
cards.text: Anthology of the Killer is a series and collection of nine horror comedy games that were developed by Irish independent game developer Stephen Gillmurphy under the pseudonyms "garmentdistrict" and "thecatamites". The nine horror games in the series were released for free on Game Jolt between 2020 and 2024, the first game being Voice of the Killer in December of 2020, before a paid collection of all nine games with bonus content was published in May 2024 for Windows, macOS, and Linux. A port to the Nintendo Switch and PS5 was later released in April of 2026. The series stars a young woman named BB, a college student and resident of a city filled with serial killers who explores her surroundings to find "spooky" content to write about for her zine. In the nine games, she ends up in bizarre and dangerous situations from her encounters with various serial killers and other creatures.

cards.heading: BB, surreal horror and a recurring heroine
cards.text: Stephen Gillmurphy created the game series due to his interest in combining humour, horror, surrealism, and mystery to tell bizarre stories about BB as a "recurring heroine". He put particular balance between the humour and horror elements, in part to create a never-ending cycle of the two. The collection's bizarre elements were further enhanced by his game design patterns, in which he combined content like the drawings' features and improvised the game's levels. The Anthology of the Killer series has been praised by critics for its comedy-horror balance and general surrealism, especially from the visuals and humorous dialogue. At the 2024 Independent Games Festival (IGF), it won the Nuovo Award and was also nominated for the Seumas McNally Grand Prize and another award for Excellence in Visual Arts.

main.title: The Game Awards
main.subtitle: A shared archive of the work we remember
main.summary: A celebration of game makers, with every category winner from 2014 onward.

cards.heading: What the awards celebrate
cards.text: The Game Awards celebrates the people who make games: designers, artists, writers, performers, composers and the teams around them. Created by Geoff Keighley in 2014, the annual show combines awards with performances, announcements and conversations about the medium.

cards.heading: A changing medium, a shared stage
cards.text: An awards archive is also a record of changing priorities. Categories make room for new ways to play and new kinds of work, from independent production and performance to accessibility and community support. Move through the years to read every category winner, then open the official ceremony beside the list.

main.title: Cyberpunk 2077
main.summary: Cyberpunk 2077 is a 2020 action role-playing game developed by CD Projekt Red and published by CD Projekt.

cards.heading: V and Johnny Silverhand in Night City
cards.text: Cyberpunk 2077 is a 2020 action role-playing game developed by CD Projekt Red and published by CD Projekt. Based on and set in the fictional universe of Mike Pondsmith's Cyberpunk tabletop game series, Cyberpunk 2077 takes place in the dystopian metropolis of Night City in California. The player assumes the role of V (voiced by Gavin Drea or Cherami Leigh depending on the player character's gender), a cybernetically-enhanced mercenary who is reluctantly imbued with an experimental "biochip" containing the engram of legendary rocker-turned-terrorist Johnny Silverhand (voiced by Keanu Reeves). As Johnny's consciousness begins overwriting V's own, the two must work together to separate from each other and save V's life by confronting the Arasaka Corporation, a powerful megacorporation acting as the de facto ruler of Night City.

cards.heading: A large production and later versions
cards.text: Full production on Cyberpunk 2077 began following the release of The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Blood and Wine (2016). The game was developed by a team of around 500 people using the REDengine 4 game engine. CD Projekt launched a new division in Wrocław, Poland, and partnered with Digital Scapes, Nvidia, Q-LOC, and Jali Research to aid the production, while Pondsmith served as a consultant. The original score was composed by Marcin Przybyłowicz, P.T. Adamczyk and Paul Leonard-Morgan, while the in-game radio also featured licensed artists. After years of anticipation, Cyberpunk 2077 was released for PlayStation 4, Stadia, Windows, and Xbox One in December 2020, followed by the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S in February 2022, the Nintendo Switch 2 in June 2025 as a launch title, and macOS in July 2025. A DLC expansion, Phantom Liberty, was released for PlayStation 5, Windows, and Xbox Series X/S in September 2023, and paired with the Nintendo Switch 2 and macOS releases.

cards.heading: A troubled launch and a gradual reappraisal
cards.text: Cyberpunk 2077 received praise from critics for its narrative, setting, and graphics. It was also widely criticised for bugs and glitches, particularly on the PlayStation 4 and Xbox One versions during their launch period. Sony removed the game from the PlayStation Store from December 2020 to June 2021 while CD Projekt rectified some of the issues. CD Projekt became subject to investigations and class-action lawsuits for its perceived attempts at downplaying the severity of the technical problems before release; the investor class action was ultimately resolved through a US$1.85 million settlement. The improvements and updates delivered by the developer since, together with the release of Phantom Liberty and the 2022 tie-in anime series Cyberpunk: Edgerunners, led to a progressive reappraisal of the game.

cards.heading: Sales, production cost and a sequel
cards.text: As of July 2026, Cyberpunk 2077 had sold over 40 million copies, making it one of the best-selling video games of all time. Its total cost to develop and market (including updates and DLC) is reportedly between $436 million and around $440 million, making it one of the most expensive video games to develop. A sequel was announced in October 2022 and is in development.

main.title: Hitman 3
main.summary: Hitman 3 is a 2021 stealth game developed and published by IO Interactive.

cards.heading: The final hunt for Providence
cards.text: Hitman 3 is a 2021 stealth game developed and published by IO Interactive. It is the eighth main installment in the Hitman video game series, the sequel to 2018's Hitman 2, and the third game in the World of Assassination trilogy. Concluding the story arc started in 2016's Hitman, the game follows genetically engineered assassin Agent 47 and his allies as they hunt down the leaders of the secretive organization Providence, which controls global affairs and was partially responsible for 47's creation and upbringing.

cards.heading: Disguises and opportunities
cards.text: A disguise changes where Agent 47 can go and what he can carry without attracting attention. Listening to conversations reveals opportunities, while mission stories guide him towards more unusual assassinations. Each large location supports several approaches, with permanent shortcuts making later visits easier to navigate. Familiarity never removes every risk: certain people can see through an outfit, and an illegal act may force a change of clothes or an escape from searching guards. The central task is to understand what looks ordinary in a particular room, then use that expectation to reach the target.

cards.heading: Above the clouds in Dubai
cards.text: For the opening mission in Dubai, Engström gave the level designers and artists several phrases, such as "an inviting beginning", "open and airy", and "on top of the world" (which is the name for the mission in the game). During development the team felt that the level was not living up to the "vertigo" and "verticality" keywords, and that the level would not give the player the feeling that they were high up on a massive skyscraper. As a result, the beginning of the mission was changed so that the player started outside of the skyscraper and working their way in, rather than starting by exiting an elevator into an atrium. IO Interactive's art director and lead environment artist visited Dubai early in development to gather reference material.

cards.heading: A murder mystery at Dartmoor
cards.text: Dartmoor puts a murder mystery inside a house that still has to work as a replayable Hitman level. The detective's disguise opens rooms that would usually require stealth, but access alone does not tell the player where to look. Early versions marked every relevant person and object, leading testers to follow icons rather than investigate. The final approach uses staff conversations and sounds such as moving paper or a draught to suggest clues. Different accusations produce different outcomes, giving a fixed mystery several ways to become useful within 47's larger assignment.
